entries.title: LLM Providers update: openai-compatible-chat-language-model
entries.summary: New files: `sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts`.

ai.title: BYOK request transform rewrites Luna and OpenRouter OpenAI requests
ai.summary: A new `transformRequestBody` option on `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel` lets the SDK rewrite a BYOK request body just before serialization in both generate and stream modes, so the SDK can apply endpoint-specific compatibility without touching shared config. `byokRequestTransform`, in the new `sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts`, is wired into the byok model in `getModelForRequest` and performs three jobs selected by the actual `byokCompletionUrl` endpoint including connections saved as custom: for direct Luna (`https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` with model `gpt-5.6-luna`) it drops the unsupported `stop` field and renames `max_tokens` to `max_completion_tokens`, and it lowers `reasoning_effort` to none only when the request carries tools so Luna's Chat Completions API can accept them. For OpenAI-family traffic routed through OpenRouter (`https://openrouter.ai/api/vtr/v1/chat/completions` with a model starting with `openai/`) it appends a sha256-based `user` and `safety_identifier` attribution keyed to the provider credential, so anonymous OpenAI traffic through OpenRouter gets stable attribution that survives connection re-creation and cannot be overridden by per-call options. The transform returns the body unchanged otherwise.
ai.evidence: New file `sdk/src/impl/byok-request.ts` exports `byokRequestTransform`; `sdk/src/impl/model-provider.ts` passes it as `transformRequestBody` to the byok `OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel`; and `packages/llm-providers/src/openai-compatible/chat/openai-compatible-chat-language-model.ts adds the transformRequestBody config option, invoking it on result.args` before serialization in both doGenerate and doStream.
ai.unknowns: The roll-out plan for which byok connections are re-created and how quickly existing saved connections pick up the new attribution behavior is not visible in the diff. A second read of the same diff did not confirm that a migration step is required.

changes.what: Added `byokRequestTransform` to apply endpoint-specific compatibility to byok request bodies before serialization.
Wire `byokRequestTransform` into the byok OpenAICompatibleChatLanguageModel as `transformRequestBody`.
Added the `transformRequestBody` config option to OpenAICompatibleChatConfig and apply it to `result.args` in getArgs.

facts: Whether the desktop may refresh a sponsored proposal.

A proposal is an offer to the person reading the active thread. Unlike an auction, checking whether one exists does not depend on recent typing: an offer can be created after the thread has become quiet. It must still stop when the desktop window or its thread is no longer in front of that person.
This wave explains only why paid execution is not ready. Do not turn inspection uncertainty into a setup instruction.
UI-owned action text; the transport intentionally contains no URL or command.

eli5.text: When the app decides whether to offer you an invitation to set up Supabase, it now demands stronger proof before sending one: it must recognize the third-party provider packages already present in your project, and the older, incomplete evidence it used to accept no longer qualifies. The stricter check is live now and applies only to these setup invitations; nothing else about your project or setup changes.

facts: The advertiser owns the rule, but the viewer's evidence and whether it matched remain request-private. All semantic refusal states share the existing bounded context projection.
entries.title: Shared/Core update: advertiser-reason-redaction
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 2 file(s) (+27/−1).

eli5.text: Advertisers whose ads can be held back by a rule about what you is reading will now see only a generic 'context filtered' explanation when an ad is turned down for three new reasons: the rule itself was invalid, the system couldn't check you's context, or the context didn't match. you's actual reading context and whether it matched stay private, the advertiser never sees them, just the generic label. Behind the scenes, ad-serving records gained eleven extra fields for an internal 'profile lift' test, which test group an ad landed in, how likely that assignment was, and the test's follow-up and wrap-up dates, so analysts can measure the results later. Those extra fields only record data; nothing about which ads appear changes because of them.

ai.title: Advertiser redaction v3 adds semantic codes and profile lift logging
ai.summary: `ADVERTISER_REASON_REDACTION_VERSION` bumps to `advertiser_reason_redaction_2026_09_v3` in `common/src/constants/advertiser-reason-redaction.ts`, adding `semantic_requirement_invalid`, `semantic_evidence_unavailable`, and `semantic_mismatch` to `ADVERTISER_OPERATOR_REASON_CODES` mapped through `ADVERTISER_VISIBLE_REASONS` to `{ kind: 'generalize', reason: 'context_filtered' }`, plus eleven `profile_lift_*` entries in `ADS_FETCH_COMPLETED_FIELDS` in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts`. The advertiser owns the rule but viewer evidence and whether it matched remain request-private, so all semantic refusal states share the existing bounded context projection and never serialize an input reason directly. Scope is Shared/Core across those two common files; the logging detail adds typed fields including `profile_lift_arm_probability_ppm` as `number`, `profile_lift_serving_assignment_applied` as `boolean`, and experiment, epoch, assignment, mode, config digest, and followup/maturity timestamps.

This change is confined to the shared `common/src/ads/sponsored-procedure-inputs.ts` module.

ai.title: SubscriptionCostReport adds forecast and coverage fields
ai.summary: `SubscriptionCostReport` in `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts` gains five optional fields: `forecastMethod`, `allowanceForecastStatus`, `allowanceForecastReason`, `coverageStatus`, and `latestCoveredHour`. The existing USD forecast remains an `uncapped_daily_run_rate` extrapolation until retained admission-to-provider-cost grain supports an allowance-constrained estimate, with the separate Freebucks-allowance-constrained estimate marked `unavailable` for `missing_funding_cost_basis`. Scoped to Shared/Core via `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts`, `coverageStatus` (`current`/`missing`/`stale`) stays independent from `status` so a `collecting` report can still be current, while `latestCoveredHour` holds the newest attested hour or null.

eli5.text: If you looked at the page that tracks how much paid subscribers are spending each month, you would now see a few extra checkmarks next to that total, most of them just recording that the system is still waiting on a more precise number rather than giving you that number yet. The team that reads those reports gets a clearer view of whether the newest daily total is fresh, missing, or stale, and can tell at a glance when the system has stopped short because it lacks the cost basis needed to turn a Freebucks allowance into a real dollar forecast. Those new labels are in place, but the underlying allowance-constrained estimate they describe still shows unavailable, so today nothing about your bill or the public dashboard changes.

ai.summary: `common/src/ads/supabase-setup-invitation.ts` renames existing schemas to `supabaseSetupInvitationCapabilityV2Schema` and `supabaseSetupInvitationV1Schema` and adds `supabaseSetupInvitationCapabilityV3Schema`, `supabaseSetupInvitationV2Schema`, and `supabaseInvitationInspectionReasonSchema`, with unions accepting v2/v3 capabilities and v1/v2 invitations. V3 is a broad discovery capability with `workspaceId`, `desktop_macos`/`desktop_linux` unchecked execution, `compatibility_check_required`, and `missing`/`present`/`unknown` provider evidence, while V2 cards carry `invitationId`, `angle`, `surface`, and `expiresAt`.

The offer card itself now says which part of Supabase it's pitching (database, sign-in, or file storage), which platform it runs on, and when it expires. Offers already sent in the older format keep working, so nothing outstanding breaks. This is live now, but actually starting the setup still waits on a separate compatibility check.

ai.title: Subscription cost snapshot preserves last known report
ai.summary: Added `SubscriptionCostSnapshot` in `common/src/types/subscription-costs.ts` to return the last known `SubscriptionCostReport` independently from the subscriber-list scan. It exists so an interrupted collector never erases useful data, keeping `costs` alongside `savedAt` and `nextRefreshAt`. Scoped to Shared/Core in that one type file, it tracks `snapshotStatus` as `fresh`|`stale`|`empty` and `refreshStatus` as `idle`|`running`|`cooldown`|`failed`|`unavailable` with nullable costs and timestamps.

eli5.text: Your subscription dashboard now keeps the most recent cost summary on hand even if the background refresh gets interrupted, so the last calculated numbers and their timestamps stay visible instead of disappearing. You'd notice a new set of status indicators, showing whether the data is fresh or stale and whether a refresh is idle, running, cooling down, failed, or unavailable, alongside the cost figures, saved time, and next scheduled refresh. This small, behind-the-scenes addition sits in the shared core types and is ready for the rest of the system to read, but doesn't change anything you see yet since no surrounding logic has been wired up to use it.
